task: r2t3 (r5t4) - D2/D3 alternatives: vertical offset vs font size, read-only
mode: read-only. No canvas write, no bridge write call, no document change. The only artifact is this JSON.
head: f939bc7
premise: t2 + r5t3 established that sliding each label along its own wire leaves an EMPTY net-clearance interval. This task changes dimension: move perpendicular (page y) or shrink the text.
criteria: 1 no overlap with any black glyph
2 still attributable to its own net: anchor-to-own-wire distance <= 6
2' the own wire must remain the nearest for the anchor AND for the ink; otherwise the label is attributable to a neighbouring net at one of the two levels
4 readability: font size may not fall below 4

measured.frameScale: 8.25 px/unit (r2t1 frames, reused so the numbers stay comparable with r5t1)

planA.idea: translate the label along page y by h so its ink leaves the pressed glyph band
planA.networkNote: the label is attached by parentPrimitiveId, so ownership is structural; d<=6 is the audit heuristic. Moving the anchor vertically raises d from 0 to h.

obj1.criterion2Literal: PASS for every h in [3.76, 6.0]: d = h <= 6
obj1.why: Up clears the digits at h>=3.76 but the INK then sits closer to the row above (MCU-33) than to its own wire, so it reads as the wrong net. Down clears them at h>=4.37 but the anchor lands within 0.1-0.6 of the +3V3 wire at y=800, so the d-rule itself assigns it to +3V3. The two directions fail on two different levels and neither leaves a usable band.

obj2.why: the tallest free black band within d<=6 is 2.07 units while the label is 3.76 units tall, so criterion 1 is unsatisfiable at every h. This is geometric, not a matter of taste.

planA.fatalPoint: the brief expected the killer at h>6. It is not: h_min is 3.76-4.37, so d stays under 6 and the label still counts as that wire's label. It breaks EARLIER, at two different places: (a) once h>2.18 the ink is nearer the neighbouring wire than its own - arithmetic: ink-to-own = 0.94+h, ink-to-MCU-33 = 5.30-h, equal at h=2.18; (b) going down, the +3V3 wire at y=800 is only 5 units below, so from h=4.37 the anchor is 0.6 from it, nearer than its own wire. The effective thresholds are therefore 2.18 (ink) and ~4.4 (anchor), both below the h needed to clear the glyph.

planB.idea: shrink fontSize so the ink narrows enough to stop covering the pressed glyph

calibration.note: ink width scales with font size. The 14pt ink came out 4.2% narrower than the linear prediction, so a linear estimate of the required size is mildly optimistic; the true size would be a few percent LARGER, which does not help a shrink-to-fit plan.

obj1.why: best case is fs 3.81 (scaling about the attribute anchor), below the floor of 4. The other origins need less: ink-left 1.62, ink-right 2.10; ink-centre is impossible at any size because the pressed glyph contains the label centre.

obj2.why: the label starts at 369.18 while PB10 spans 368.21-385.30, i.e. the glyph covers the label's left edge. Left-pinned shrinking can never move that edge out; centre-pinned is impossible (centre inside the glyph); anchor-pinned needs fs <= 2.85. All below the floor of 4.

floor.rationale: every visible net label on this page is fs 6 (55 wire + 14 flag). At 8.25 px/unit its ink is 3.76 units tall; at fs 4 it would be 2.51 units (~21 px), already shorter than the pin numbers beside it (4.36-4.85 units). Below 4 the net name becomes the smallest text in its row, subordinate to the number it is meant to name - the fix would swap a collision for a legibility defect. This is a judgement and is labelled as one.

overall: BOTH plans are no-go for BOTH labels. Under the current constraints (d<=6, fs>=4) D2/D3 cannot be fixed by moving the label off the wire or by shrinking it.
recommendation: Register D2 (attr111 / MCU-34 over pin number 31) and D3 (attr43 / MCU-26 flag name over PB10) as known defects. Do not relax d<=6, do not shrink below 4, do not move a label onto the neighbouring row.

D3 has no geometric room at all (tallest gap 2.07 vs label 3.76). D2 has vertical room but every position that clears the digits mis-assigns the label - at the ink level going up, at the anchor level going down.

The real fix is upstream and out of scope here: the row pitch is 10 units while the label ink is 3.76 and the pin numbers 4.36-4.85, so a label and a number cannot share a 10-unit row without touching. Either the pin-number placement rule or the row pitch has to change - a layout decision for the host, not a label tweak.
